newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds at lower levels late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds at lower levels late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held at lower levels late Monday in lackluster trade, still pressured by milder Northeast and Midwest weather forecasts this week though technical buying kept prices above support.
At 1435 EDT, August was still down by 2.3 cents at $2.08 per million British thermal units, while September was 1.3 cents lower at $2.095. Others were down by 0.9 to 1.8 cents.

"We could see a brief rally (in July) to the $2.15 area, but I'm not sure it will stay there. With some nukes coming back and the (mild) weather, I think there's a lot of people looking to sell it," said one Texas-based trader.
While forecasts this week for milder Northeast and Midwest weather helped trigger the early selloff, traders noted prices have held fairly steady since the open.
And opinions remained divided about market direction, with some expecting downside to be limited by the seven-cent cash premium to paper and some seasonal heat in southern tier states.
"The market should be cratering (because of the weather), but it isn't," said an East Coast trader.

While technical traders said August's brief dip Monday below the double bottom at $2.065 could trigger some pressure, most saw the $2.055 spot continuation low from June 12 as a more significant support point. Psychological support was seen ahead of $2. Resistance was pegged at $2.11, $2.15 and then along the down trendline at about $2.26. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents to about the $2.10 level. Midcon pipes stayed little changed in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas also was quoted a couple of cents higher in the high-$2.30s.
NYMEX said 15,715 contracts traded at 1405 EDT. Hub open interest on July 3 rose 1,133 contracts to 199,564.
On the KCBT, August fell 1.2 cents to $1.96, while deferreds were steady to 2.5 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 12.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
